title: Universal Fintype Induction Principle
description: A unified framework for 'induction on size' for all finite mathematical objects. Well-founded induction on any measure function f : α → ℕ provides a universal induction principle that recovers Finset.induction, List.induction, and structural induction on graphs, matroids, etc. as special cases.

meta.assumptions: None. All theorems are fully proved using Lean's built-in well-founded induction.

overview.historicalContext: Structural induction on data types (lists, trees, Finsets) is well-established in type theory. The question is whether a single principle can unify induction across all finite mathematical structures — graphs, matroids, polytopes, etc. The answer is yes: well-founded induction on any measure function provides the general framework.
overview.problemStatement: Can a unified framework formalize 'induction on size' for all finite mathematical objects via a universal Fintype induction principle?
overview.text: Yes. Well-founded induction on any measure function f : α → ℕ gives a universal induction principle. For Finsets, use card; for lists, use length; for graphs, use vertex count.
overview.proofStrategy: Show that `WellFounded.induction` on the inverse image of `<` under any measure `f : α → ℕ` provides induction for arbitrary types. Then demonstrate recovering Finset.induction as a special case.
keyInsights: Any function f : α → ℕ gives well-founded induction via InvImage.wf
Finset.induction is the special case where f = Finset.card
The framework extends to any finite mathematical structure with a notion of 'size'
Lean's WellFoundedRelation typeclass makes this generic

sections.title: Measure-Based Induction

conclusion.text: Well-founded induction on measure functions provides a universal framework for induction on finite mathematical objects. The specific measure depends on the structure, but the principle is the same: InvImage.wf lifts well-foundedness of < on ℕ to any type.
conclusion.implications: Any formalization involving finite structures can use this pattern.

crossReferences.description: Generalizes the parent's induction principles to all finite mathematical structures

mainTheorems.name: measure_induction
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ (f : α → ℕ) (P : α → Prop), (∀ x, (∀ y, f y < f x → P y) → P x) → ∀ x, P x
